questions.question: What are the three levels of reading?
questions.explanation: The three levels are literal (what the text says), inferential (what it implies) and evaluative (what you think about it).

questions.question: What does it mean to make an inference?
options: Combining text evidence with background knowledge to understand what is implied
Copying a sentence from the text
questions.explanation: An inference combines clues in the text with your background knowledge to reach meaning that is not directly stated.

questions.question: Which levels do most exam questions target?
questions.explanation: You are rarely asked to just find a fact — most exam questions require reading between the lines and critical evaluation.

questions.question: "The character walks slowly, suggesting reluctance." Which reading level is this?
options: Inferential — interpreting what the text implies
Literal — stating what the text says
No level — it is a grammar comment
questions.explanation: Interpreting the slow walk as a sign of reluctance reads between the lines — the inferential level.

questions.question: What must always support an inference in an exam answer?
options: Your general feelings about the topic
A quote from a different book
questions.explanation: A valid inference always points to specific textual evidence — ask yourself why the author included a detail.
